messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a bunch of traces where spans stop at the gateway and never show up in the async worker traces. Happening after the rabbit->kafka migration for async jobs. Any quick theories? :thinking:

ajay: Is the gateway injecting W3C tracecontext headers into the message metadata or body? We switched propagators recently.

maria: We thought so. Gateway uses the OTEL SDK and `traceparent` header in HTTP -> we copy headers into rabbit message properties `headers` map. On the consumer side, the worker reads headers and tries to extract. But when messages are batched we sometimes see `traceparent` missing or malformed.

kevin: Common pattern: message brokers that batch/re-serialize can drop or canonicalize header keys (e.g., uppercase vs lowercase). Are we normalizing keys on publish+consume?

maria: Not explicitly. Rabbit client sets whatever we pass. I noticed some messages had `traceparent` and some had `Traceparent` when we dumped raw frames.

lina: Also watch for propagator mismatch. We moved from b3 -> w3c a while back. If some services still inject b3 we need multi-propagator support. OTEL has `CompositePropagator`.

ajay: Agreed. Another gotcha: when you put trace context in message body vs properties. Our Node consumer reads only properties. If a legacy producer embeds `x-trace` in the JSON body, it will get lost.

maria: Good point. The kafka side of the pipeline uses message headers, but there's a transform lambda in between that serializes to Avro and drops unknown header types. Could be the culprit.

sam: For async queues, if you can't carry full context, create a new span and add the original trace id as a link. That preserves correlation without forcing strict context continuation. Example (pseudo):
```
// on worker
ctx = propagation.extract(carrier)
if !ctx.valid {
  // create new root span but link to previous
  link := trace.Link{SpanContext: trace.SpanContextFromHex(orig_trace_id)}
  span := tracer.Start(ctx, "process_job", trace.WithLinks(link))
} else {
  span := tracer.Start(ctx, "process_job")
}
```

kevin: Nice. Links are great for retries or when you lose sampling flags. Also ensure we propagate `baggage` if teams rely on tenant_id, request_id etc.

maria: One operational issue: traces are present in Jaeger for fast requests but worker spans show up separately with a different trace id. That makes end-to-end latency hard to read.

lina: Can we canonicalize on a single propagation strategy: HTTP/gateway -> put `traceparent` + `otlp-trace` header in message metadata (stringified) and also set `correlation_id` top-level property? That gives redundancy.

ajay: I pushed a small change to add `correlation_id` (UUID) and `traceparent` into headers for all outgoing async events. But we need consumers to prefer `traceparent` if present, else fallback to `correlation_id`->link.

maria: Also found one more: our OTLP exporter batching in the gateway is aggressive — spans for short-lived requests sometimes get exported after the worker already processed job, so timeline looks odd. We should set exporter flush interval lower for gateway spans or use synchronous flush on handoff span.

kevin: For OTLP exporter config: lower `schedule_delay_millis` to 100ms for gateway service handoff spans. For workers, keep batch bigger. But watch for CPU overhead.

lina: We should also add a small handoff span that wraps serialization + publish; that span should include the traceparent header string as an attribute so even if propagation fails downstream the logs/trace can be correlated. Example attribute: `handoff.traceparent = "traceparent-value"`.

sam: TL;DR actionable items: 
- normalize header keys on publish & consumer (maria)
- update intermediate Avro transformer to preserve headers or move trace to body (ajay)
- implement CompositePropagator and fallback logic (kevin)
- add correlation_id redundancy and handoff span attribute (maria)
- lower OTLP exporter flush for gateway handoff spans (lina)

maria: I'm on normalize + correlation_id. Will open PRs today.

ajay: I'll look at the Avro transformer and Kafka consumer fallback.

tracebot: deploy-bot: New tracing config PR detected on `infra/tracing` (PR #442). CI passed. :white_check_mark:

maria: Thanks. Once PRs land let's run the consumer with debug logging on propagation for 24h and re-check traces in Kibana + Jaeger.

kevin: One last note — long retention for traces is expensive. If we start linking instead of continuing traces for async jobs we can keep parent traces high-fidelity and store worker traces with shorter retention and index by correlation_id for on-demand lookup. That reduces storage without sacrificing debugability.

lina: Good plan. I'll draft a doc for retention tiers: 30d for end-to-end traces, 7d for worker-only traces, keep index for correlation_id 90d.

maria: Perfect. Thanks all. I'll post PR links here when ready.
